name: Squad Delivery
description: Delivery flow for the agenfk-squad agents (https://github.com/eduardopin/agenfk-squad). Each step names the agent that owns it and the evidence `agenfk verify` must carry: product cuts the card, developer/frontend/infra implement in one worktree per card, tester proves the tests can fail, an independent verifier reviews, attacks and mutates, and only the main session advances the card. Whoever writes does not approve.
author: eduardopin

steps.name: TODO
steps.label: To Do
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the `product` agent (read-only). The card states the smallest increment a real user can use, lists acceptance criteria that can be checked by running something, names the files or areas it is expected to touch, and lists the cards it depends on. A card that does not fit in about 120k tokens of context is split before it leaves TODO. When two or more cards will run in parallel in the same repository, the `github` agent has delivered the map (session -> worktree -> branch -> card) and the fronts touch disjoint files. Evidence for `agenfk verify`: the acceptance criteria as written on the card and, for parallel work, the worktree path and branch of this card.

steps.name: IMPLEMENT
steps.label: Implement
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the `developer` agent (or `frontend` for anything that changes how the product looks, moves or is used; `infra` for Terraform, CI and Dockerfiles, which stops at `plan`). One card = one branch = one worktree = one session. The agent calls `agenfk gatekeeper --item-id <id>` before the first edit, works only inside the card's worktree, keeps the change to what the card asks, and commits on the card's branch. It never opens a PR, merges, applies or deploys. The project's own suite passes in the worktree. Evidence for `agenfk verify`: branch name, commit SHAs, the suite command and its result as run by the agent (counts, exit code), and anything the card asked for that was left out.

steps.name: TEST
steps.label: Test
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the `tester` agent, in a separate session from the one that wrote the code. It edits test files only. Tests cover the happy path, the edges and the failure modes named in the acceptance criteria; a defect found by running the system becomes a regression test. For each new test the agent shows it can fail: it breaks the production code the test targets, watches the test go red, and restores the code. Evidence for `agenfk verify`: the list of tests added, the suite command and result, and for each new test the mutation applied and the failure it produced.

steps.name: REVIEW
steps.label: Review
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the `verifier` agent, read-only, in a clean context. Whoever wrote the code does not approve it: brief the verifier with the card id and the branch, never with the implementer's account of the work. The verifier reads the diff against the acceptance criteria, runs the suite itself, and returns SHIP, FIX_FIRST or REJECT with each finding tied to a file and line. FIX_FIRST and REJECT go back to the agent that implemented, for at most two rounds; after that the decision is the owner's. Evidence for `agenfk verify`: the verdict, the suite result as run by the verifier, the findings and which of them were fixed or rejected and why.

steps.name: ADVERSARIAL
steps.label: Adversarial
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the `verifier` agent, in a fresh session, trying to break the change rather than confirm it: inputs outside the happy path, concurrency and ordering, failure of each dependency, authorization and injection, regressions in the callers of what changed, and integration with the rest of the system actually run, not read. The verifier never fixes what it finds. Evidence for `agenfk verify`: each attack tried and its outcome (what was run, what happened), and the verdict SHIP, FIX_FIRST or REJECT.

steps.name: MUTATE
steps.label: Mutate
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the `verifier` agent. It mutates the production code changed by the card (flip a condition, drop a branch, change a boundary, remove a call) one mutation at a time, runs the suite, and restores the tree after each one. A mutation that survives is a missing test and goes back to the `tester`. The working tree is clean at the end (`git status --short` is empty). Evidence for `agenfk verify`: the mutations applied, killed versus survived, and the tests added for the survivors.

steps.name: VERIFY
steps.label: Verify
steps.exitCriteria: Owner: the main session, which is the only one that advances a card. It checks every acceptance criterion against something that was run, not against a summary: the criterion, the command, the observed result. When the flow asks for a PR, only the `github` agent opens it, and only after the verifier returned SHIP. Merging to the main branch goes through the merge queue: `squad-turn request <PR>`, and on MERGE TURN one `git fetch`, one `git merge origin/main`, the suite, push, merge. Evidence for `agenfk verify`: the criterion-by-criterion table, the PR URL if one exists, and the token cost of the card (`agenfk tokens`).
